warnings.details: Rewrite in the Bank's own voice; remove report-machinery phrases: available evidence

main_issues: Required structure: the draft does not present the full 'Emirates-style' nine-heading General Requirements chapter as required by the evaluation principles (it includes many, but not clearly all nine as discrete required headings; additionally, some IFRS S1 general requirements items like identification of the related financial statements/reporting period are not concretely stated because period fields are null).

Sources of guidance subsection overreaches relative to evidence: evidence package provides no documented sources_of_guidance; the draft should be framed as the Bank’s chosen approach rather than implying a documented framework selection process.

Assurance wording risks misleading users because operational GHG records are not available in the evidence package; the draft should clearly state whether Scope 1/2 emissions are disclosed in this report and, if not, that they are outside scope / not yet quantified here.
Material transparency omission: the report-level boundary that synthetic/generated data is used is not disclosed.
required_fixes: Add an explicit basis-of-preparation transparency statement that the report includes synthetic/generated elements (consistent with report_level_boundaries.uses_synthetic_or_generated_data=true), and clarify which parts are modelled/estimated.

Revise the 'Sources of guidance' subsection to avoid implying documented applied guidance beyond IFRS S1/S2; state plainly that the report uses an IFRS S1/S2-style structure and that SASB topics/metrics have not been applied in this report (as already stated), without implying other frameworks were assessed/applied.

Tighten assurance disclosure: explicitly state whether Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions are disclosed in this report; if not, state that operational emissions disclosures are not included / not yet quantified in this report, while noting that any limited assurance undertaken (if any) relates only to selected Scope 1/2 metrics outside/within the report scope.

Where the draft uses conditional comparative language ('may be provided'), align it with what the Bank actually discloses (given trend metrics are available per known_evidence_boundaries) or explicitly state that comparatives are not included in this report despite being available.

Ensure the General Requirements chapter presents the required headings as discrete subsections (and, once known, identify the related financial statements and reporting period to satisfy IFRS S1 timing/period linkage expectations).
unsupported_claims: “The Bank applies the concepts and structure of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 as the primary framing for these disclosures.” (Generally plausible, but not evidenced by a formal basis-of-preparation statement or mapping; acceptable if kept as 'intended' framing.)

“The Bank currently uses modelled estimates and proxies for [scenario analysis, financed emissions and sector-level portfolio views].” (Scenario outputs are modelled estimates per boundaries; financed emissions availability is true, but 'proxies' and 'sector-level portfolio views' are not evidenced in this General Requirements package and should be framed more cautiously.)

“Any external assurance activities that the Bank undertakes… relate to selected Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions only.” (Assurance evidence exists and scope1_scope2_assurance_only=true, but the draft also implies environmental metrics assurance activities exist without specifying whether assured metrics are included in this report.)

“Trend metrics on Board and committee activity, climate expertise and climate-linked remuneration are intended to provide insight…” (Evidence indicates such trend metrics exist, but the draft’s comparative section says they 'may be provided', creating ambiguity about whether they are actually disclosed.)
material_unsupported_claims: “This subsection explains the main sources of guidance used to frame the Bank’s… disclosures.” followed by “No other formal disclosure frameworks… are described as having been applied…” — the evidence package lists sources_of_guidance as empty. The draft should not imply a documented selection of guidance beyond IFRS S1/S2 unless the Bank explicitly states it; reframe to: 'This report is prepared using an IFRS S1/S2-style structure; the Bank has not applied SASB topics/metrics in this report.'

Implied assurance positioning: stating limited external assurance exists for selected Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions without clarifying whether those Scope 1/2 emissions are disclosed in this report (operational_ghg_records_available=false). This can mislead users; must clarify the boundary (e.g., 'Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions are not disclosed in this report / are outside scope / are under development', if that is the Bank’s position).
minor_wording_to_tighten: “intended to be read as a dedicated chapter of a bank-focused sustainability report” — acceptable, but could be tightened to avoid implying publication form if not specified elsewhere.

“The report is designed to complement, and be read alongside, the Bank’s general purpose financial statements.” — acceptable, but IFRS S1 also expects identification of the related financial statements; consider explicitly identifying them (e.g., 'the consolidated financial statements for the year ended …') once reporting period is known.
Comparatives: repeated use of “may be provided” could be tightened to “are provided where available” to align with the stated policy, unless the Bank truly does not include them.
available_evidence_omitted: Report-level boundary that synthetic/generated data is used (report_level_boundaries.uses_synthetic_or_generated_data=true) is not disclosed in the General Requirements draft.

Known evidence boundary that operational GHG records are not available (operational_ghg_records_available=false) is not explicitly stated; the draft implies Scope 1/2 assurance may exist without stating whether Scope 1/2 figures are disclosed in this report.

Known evidence boundary that methodology records are not available (methodology_records_available=false) is not explicitly stated in the General Requirements section (only general 'estimates and proxies' wording is used).

Governance evidence availability for trend metrics (e.g., board climate expertise %, climate on board agenda %, remuneration linkage %) is not referenced as being available; the draft uses conditional language ('may be provided') rather than stating what is actually disclosed.

main_issues: Management/risk-register content is generally well used, but several mitigation-action statements read like confirmed, operating controls rather than ‘actions recorded in the register’, creating over-claim risk.
One risk-register numeric example is framed with an ‘estimated potential’ qualifier that is not evidenced as the register’s defined measure.
Some governance/control phrasing implies a more formalised ERM linkage and governance-control system than is evidenced (beyond the ERM-integration flag and semi-annual reporting).
required_fixes: Reframe the mitigation actions list explicitly as “mitigation actions recorded in the climate risk register” and avoid implying bank-wide implementation or operating effectiveness unless separately evidenced.

Adjust the EUR 165.2 million example to match the evidence neutrally (e.g., “recorded financial impact of EUR 165.2 million”); avoid adding qualifiers like “estimated potential” unless that wording is evidenced.
Tighten ERM linkage language to the evidenced fact pattern: keep the ERM-integration flag statement (6 of 8) and avoid broader claims about integration into ERM processes beyond what is stated.

Keep TCFD/IFRS S2 alignment as an indicator flag in the final boundaries subsection and avoid implying governance ‘verifies’ alignment (the draft largely does this correctly; just ensure no implied assurance/control language elsewhere).
unsupported_claims: “ERM integration indicators show that climate-related risks are linked to the Bank’s enterprise risk management processes for a subset of recorded risks.” (partly supported by ERM-integration flags, but ‘linked to ERM processes’ is stronger than evidenced)

“Governance arrangements support the oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities described in the strategy, risk management and metrics and targets sections…” (generic linkage; not directly evidenced in the compact governance evidence)
material_unsupported_claims: Risk register example: “...associated with an estimated potential financial impact of EUR 165.2 million.” Evidence supports EUR 165.2 million, but the draft labels it “estimated potential financial impact” without confirming the register uses that exact definition; should be stated neutrally as “financial impact of EUR 165.2 million (as recorded in the register)” or similar.

Mitigation actions list includes items that are evidenced as labels in the register, but the draft presents them as implemented controls (e.g., “engagement and transition-plan covenants with borrowers”, “sector exposure limits and enhanced due diligence”). Without additional control-design/operating-effectiveness evidence, these should be framed as “recorded mitigation actions” rather than implying they are fully implemented bank-wide controls.

Overview: “climate checks for major transactions” is supported as an activity indicator, but the surrounding phrasing implies a more formalised control framework (“ERM integration indicators”, “climate checks”, “risk register” presented as a cohesive governance-control system). Needs tightening to avoid implying a formal control system beyond what is evidenced.
minor_wording_to_tighten: “These indicators show that climate-related matters were regularly considered at Board level.” (reasonable inference from agenda coverage; could be softened to “indicate”)

“The committee’s role in climate-related oversight is therefore described on the basis of its meeting frequency and recorded climate-related agenda coverage.” (acceptable, but could be simplified to avoid sounding methodological)

“The Bank operates a skills development programme that includes climate-related topics.” (supported as programme existence; could clarify it is a programme including climate topics, without implying breadth/mandatory coverage)
available_evidence_omitted: 2024 governance alignment flags (TCFD aligned = true; IFRS S2 aligned = true) are not explicitly stated as indicators in the final boundaries subsection (draft states them, but not clearly as indicator flags and includes an over-strong implication elsewhere).

main_issues: Targets wording overreaches the ‘target summary only’ boundary by implying alignment/validation detail (SBTi 1.5°C alignment phrasing; ‘net-zero banking framework’ phrasing) without disclosing the underlying assumptions/dependencies.

Financial effects disclosure is strong on exposures, scenario-modelled impacts and resource allocation indicators, but does not clearly and explicitly state that current-period financial statement impacts (and material adjustment risk to carrying amounts) have not been separately quantified/disclosed.
One physical risk from the risk register is omitted despite physical risk evidence being available and the Strategy positioning itself as covering material risks.
Report-machinery language appears (“The evidence does not provide enough detail …”), which is a material wording defect under the required reporting voice.
required_fixes: Rewrite all report-machinery phrasing into the Bank’s voice (e.g., replace “The evidence does not provide enough detail …” with “The Bank does not currently disclose … / has not yet assessed …”).

Targets: Reframe target statements to stay within target-summary availability. Avoid implying external validation or detailed methodological alignment; keep to: target type, scope, target year, referenced framework name, status (‘on track’) and progress percentage. Do not add baselines, milestones, gross/net, credits, or validation assertions.

Financial effects: Add an explicit boundary that the Bank has not separately quantified/disclosed (i) current-period impacts on financial position/performance/cash flows attributable to climate-related risks/opportunities and (ii) risks of material adjustment to carrying amounts within the next annual reporting period. Keep scenario outputs clearly separated as modelled estimates.
Include the third physical risk from the climate risk register (or explicitly state that only selected top risks are presented here and where the full register is disclosed).

Capex/opex wording: Clarify upfront that ‘climate-related capex/opex’ are internal indicators of resource allocation and are not necessarily aligned to financial statement capex/opex classifications or presented as separate line items.
unsupported_claims: “We use short‑, medium‑ and long‑term time horizons consistent with our risk register and scenario analysis, and we link these to our planning and capital management processes.” (Linkage to planning/capital management processes is asserted but not evidenced beyond general statements.)

“All three targets are currently assessed as on track, with progress of 40.0%, 25.0% and 13.3% respectively in 2024.” (Progress and on-track status are supported, but the surrounding target wording introduces unsupported specificity—see material items.)

“We have adopted … an absolute reduction target for Scope 1 and 2 emissions aligned with an SBTi 1.5°C pathway by 2030 …” (Alignment/validation nuance risks over-precision given only target summary availability.)

“In 2024, climate-related capital expenditure amounted to EUR 476.95 million and climate-related operating expenditure amounted to EUR 219.32 million.” (Amounts are supported, but labelling as ‘capital expenditure’ and ‘operating expenditure’ can be read as financial-statement capex/opex classification; the draft later clarifies they are not separate line items, but the initial phrasing is still potentially misleading.)

“Our portfolio metrics … indicate areas where climate-related risks may affect expected credit losses, risk‑weighted assets and funding costs over time.” (Directional statement is plausible but not supported with quantified ECL/RWA/funding-cost effects.)
Report-machinery phrasing: “The evidence does not provide enough detail to assess full operational adaptation capacity …” (Must be rewritten in the Bank’s own voice.)
material_unsupported_claims: Targets: “aligned with an SBTi 1.5°C pathway” and “under a net‑zero banking framework” are presented as alignment/validation-style claims. With only target summary available, the Strategy should avoid implying external validation/assurance or detailed methodological alignment beyond naming the referenced framework (e.g., ‘using an SBTi 1.5°C pathway’ / ‘under the NZBA framework’) and should not imply SBTi validation or detailed conformance.

Financial effects (current period): The Strategy does not provide supported disclosure of how climate-related risks/opportunities affected financial position/performance/cash flows for the reporting period (it provides exposures, modelled scenario outputs, and capex/opex indicators, but not actual current-period effects). As written, it risks being read as meeting the ‘current financial effects’ requirement without actually providing them; this needs an explicit boundary statement that current-period financial statement impacts have not been separately quantified/disclosed.
minor_wording_to_tighten: “Scenario analysis under the NGFS v4 framework informs our understanding of potential financial effects …” (Tighten to avoid implying direct incorporation into financial statements.)
“Transition risk losses remain within our internal capital buffer thresholds.” (Keep as scenario-specific model output; consider adding ‘in our modelling’ to avoid sounding like an observed fact.)
“Near‑term resilience is acceptable …” (Add ‘based on our scenario analysis’ to keep it explicitly bounded.)
available_evidence_omitted: Risk register includes additional physical risks beyond flood and wildfire (physical risk count is 3); the third physical risk is not reflected in the Strategy narrative.

Scenario methodology summary includes specific notes by scenario type (orderly/disorderly/hot house) that could be stated more compactly (e.g., country-varying carbon prices in disorderly scenarios; NDC carbon pricing ramp-up from 2030).

main_issues: One over-claim about prioritising climate risks relative to other material risks without describing (or evidencing) the mechanism by which climate risks are compared across the full risk universe.
A few phrases could be tightened to anchor statements explicitly to the climate risk register (to avoid implying broader coverage than disclosed).
required_fixes: Reframe the cross-risk prioritisation statement: limit it to prioritisation within the climate risk register, and/or explicitly state that the Bank does not currently disclose how climate risks are prioritised relative to other risk types in the overall risk universe beyond the ERM integration flags.
Tighten mitigation-action wording to clearly anchor it to the climate risk register (e.g., “recorded in the climate risk register for each risk”).

Optional (not required): add one sentence quantifying ERM integration as 75% (6 of 8) and/or provide examples of NGFS scenario names used to improve reader interpretability without adding unevidenced process detail.
unsupported_claims: “Mitigation actions are recorded for the risks disclosed in this report.” (The evidence supports mitigation actions recorded in the climate risk register; the draft’s phrasing could be read as broader than the register.)

“These indicative financial impacts … are used to prioritise climate-related risks relative to one another and to other material risks.” (Evidence supports prioritisation within the register; prioritisation relative to other risk types is not evidenced beyond a general statement.)
material_unsupported_claims: “These indicative financial impacts, together with the qualitative ratings and time horizons, are used to prioritise climate-related risks relative to one another and to other material risks.” (Over-claims integration into cross-risk prioritisation; the payload does not evidence how climate risks are prioritised relative to other risk types within overall risk taxonomy/ERM beyond an integration flag.)
minor_wording_to_tighten: “Mitigation actions are recorded for the risks disclosed in this report.” → tighten to “Mitigation actions are recorded in the climate risk register for each of the eight climate-related risks.”
“We identify climate-related risks through our risk register process …” → acceptable, but could clarify that the register is the primary mechanism disclosed (not necessarily the only mechanism used).

“Any upstream implications … are considered indirectly through the transition and reputational risks recorded in the climate risk register …” → defensible, but could clarify this is not a distinct upstream process.
available_evidence_omitted: ERM integration percentage (6 of 8 = 75%) is not stated explicitly (draft states 6 of 8, but not the percentage).
Scenario analysis evidence includes named NGFS v4 scenario names (e.g., Net Zero 2050, Current Policies, Delayed Transition) that are not referenced in the narrative.
Scenario analysis evidence indicates scenario links used by risks are SCN0002, SCN0004, SCN0011, SCN0013 (draft does not list the identifiers; it refers to 'scenario identifiers' generally).

main_issues: Target validation/framework references are still too easy to read as externally validated/endorsed targets rather than internal target-record fields.

IFRS S2 GHG cross-industry metric category is boundary-disclosed (good), but the draft does not explicitly state that Scope 1/2/3 measurement approach (e.g., GHG Protocol) is not disclosed—this is implied via ‘records unavailable’ but could be made clearer to avoid perceived omission.

Financed emissions are disclosed as a single loans figure; the draft appropriately discloses the lack of perimeter detail, but the opening ‘covers portfolio emissions’ wording slightly overstates completeness.
required_fixes: Reframe all ‘third-party validation’ statements to avoid implying external assurance/approval. Use wording such as: ‘The Bank’s internal target record flags the target as third-party validated and identifies [body]; the Bank does not provide further detail in this report.’

Reframe ‘framework’ statements similarly: ‘The target record references [SBTi 1.5°C / NZBA] as the framework’ and avoid any implication of confirmed alignment, acceptance, or membership-based validation.
Tighten the Overview sentence ‘It covers portfolio emissions…’ to reflect the disclosed boundary (single financed-emissions figure for loans; perimeter not disclosed).

Optionally add one explicit sentence in the operational GHG subsection clarifying that, because operational emissions are not quantified, the Bank also does not disclose the measurement approach/inputs/assumptions for operational emissions for 2024.
unsupported_claims: “The disclosures are prepared with reference to IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 …” (general compliance-style framing without specifying what is and is not covered; acceptable only if clearly positioned as ‘prepared with reference’ and not as full compliance).
Target ‘Third-party validation’ statements risk being read as assurance/validation of the Bank’s targets rather than a target-record field, even though later limitations attempt to narrow this.
material_unsupported_claims: “Third-party validation: … SBTi identified as the validation body” / “UNEP FI identified as the validation body” presented as if the targets are validated by those bodies. The only supported fact is that the target record flags third_party_validated=true and names a validation body; this must be framed more explicitly as ‘recorded in the target record’ and not as an external validation conclusion.

“Framework: … SBTi 1.5°C pathway” and “NZBA … framework” could be interpreted as confirmed alignment/acceptance by those initiatives. Without methodology/acceptance evidence, this must be framed strictly as the framework field in the target record (not as confirmed alignment or membership-based validation).
minor_wording_to_tighten: “It covers portfolio emissions …” could be tightened to avoid implying full portfolio coverage, because the financed-emissions perimeter is explicitly not disclosed.

“These metrics are used internally to … inform risk management, client engagement and strategic planning.” (fine, but could be tightened to avoid implying systematic integration across all processes without further support).
“Climate-related capital expenditure … directed towards climate-related initiatives …” and similar for opex: acceptable, but could be tightened given the absence of classification methodology detail.

warnings.details: Prefer validation/verification wording in Metrics and targets.
